Vikram Singh: Quick proposal: let's try a different remediation cadence. Instead of 7/30/90, what about a 14/45/180 sprint model for action items? Slightly longer windows for infra/model work.

Vikram Singh: Card fields: Owner / Backup / Priority / ETA(14/45/180) / Ack SLA (72h) / Verification steps + verifier / Rollback / Observability changes / Recurrence tag / Escalation path / Status

Helena Morris: Interesting. I like a 72h ack SLA for larger infra work. can we also add an "effort" tag (small/medium/large) so PMs know resource needs?

Omar Diaz: +1 on effort tag. Suggest automated nudges at 14d and 45d, and a mandatory review meeting if something hits 180d unresolved. Also, for recurrence detection, flag items that match the same RCA keywords across incidents.

Zoe Park: For IC rotation, propose 8-week rotations with a 3-day shadow overlap. incoming IC should get a 30-min handoff slot + a one-page summary: open remediations, active alerts, recent RCA tags.

Helena Morris: Comms cadence idea: internal follow-up note within 48h, product-team sync within 72h, and a short summary added to the customer-facing status page only if SLA-blind customers are affected. Weekly remediation scoreboard in our channel showing overdue counts by team.

Vikram Singh: Volunteers? Helena can do the scoreboard mock, Omar can prototype the recurrence tagger query, Zoe can draft the IC handoff one-pager. I'll assemble a remediation card template with the effort tag and ack SLA.

incident-bot: Created doc: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/remediation-14-45-180-v1 (edit: eng-oncall)

ops-bot: Poll: "Playbook review cadence" (options: weekly / biweekly / monthly). please vote.

Helena Morris: I'll drop a scoreboard mock in the doc by Thu.

Omar Diaz: I'll push a tracker query prototype by Fri EOD to surface RCA keyword matches and recurrence counts.

Zoe Park: I'll write the 1-pager handoff and a 5-point pairing checklist for the overlap days.

Vikram Singh: Plan: pilot the 14/45/180 card on next postmortem and run the scoreboard for a month. If overdue items don't go down, we iterate. Thanks all :raised_hands:
